ORAL JUDGMENT:
1.

This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "M.V. Act") by the Insurance Company of the Motorcar, which was being driven by the deceased at the time of motor vehicular accident.

This Appeal is against the Judgment and Award dated 08.07.2003, passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Yavatmal ("MACT" for short) in Claim Petition No.103/1995, holding both the vehicles responsible for the accident.
2. The aforesaid Claim Petition was preferred by the Respondent nos.1 and 2, who are the parents of the deceased Ramesh.
On 25th May, 1994, the deceased was driving the Motorcar bearing No.MZU-4030, which was insured with the Appellant - Insurance Company.
He was going from Karanja to Pandharkawada.

When the car reached near the Sankatmochan Temple at Pandharkawada at 12.15 p.m. a Truck bearing No.CIE-1415 insured with the Respondent no.5 - Insurance Company was coming from the opposite direction and it gave dash to the Car.
Deceased suffered severe injuries and he died.

The accident was reported to 3 FA97.2011.odt the Pandharkawada Police Station and Crime came to be registered against the Driver of the Truck under the relevant sections of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") and M.V. Act.
The Claim Petition was contested by the Appellant - Insurance Company.
They contended that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Truck.
The learned Tribunal framed issues on the basis of pleadings.
In support of the Claim, the Claimant no.2 examined himself.
The Claimants brought on record the police papers in support of their Claim Petition.

Appreciating the evidence available on record, the learned Tribunal held that, the accident was the result of contributory negligence by the deceased and by the Truck Driver and held the Driver, the Owner and the Insurer of the Truck jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs. 62,500/- with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of application till its realisation.
3. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, the offence for rash and negligent was registered against the Truck Driver.
The Truck Driver was the party - Respondent no.2 before the learned Tribunal.
The Driver did not step into the witness box to show that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Car of the deceased.
The spot panchanama shows that, the car was severally damaged and there 4 FA97.2011.odt was damage to the driver side of the Truck, which goes to show the negligence of the Truck Driver.
The learned Tribunal has misinterpreted the material on record.
Therefore, the aspect of contributory negligence needs interference.
Hence, the Appeal be allowed.
4. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for Respondent no.5 - Insurance Company that, the Truck Driver himself had gone to the concerned Police Station and reported the accident.
It is submitted that, the spot panchanama do not show that, the Truck Driver was responsible for the accident.

learned Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence available on record and no interference was called for in the impugned Judgment and Award.

5. None for the Respondent nos.1, 2, 4 and 6, though served.
6.

Undisputedly, the Car, which was being driven by the deceased was insured with the Appellant Insurance Company and the Truck, which was involved in the accident was insured with Respondent no.5 - Insurance Company.
It is the matter of record that, the Respondent no.5 - Insurance Company and the Truck Driver did not contest the Claim Petition.
Undisputedly, none of the Claimants had witnessed the accident.
The Claimants relied on the police papers in support of the Claim Petition.

In the 5 FA97.2011.odt cross-examination of the Claimant no.2, who examined himself as witness, it has come that, the deceased was not at fault and their Claim was mainly against the Driver, the Owner and the Insurer of the Truck.
Admission is brought in the cross-examination of the Claimant no.2 by the Appellant that, the deceased was driving his car in slow speed and on the left side of the road.
The Claimant no.2
, was not cross-
examined by the any of the Respondents except the Appellant.
Undisputedly, Crime was registered against the Driver of the Truck, who was Respondent no.1 in the Claim Petition.
Since, he did not appear though served, the Claim Petition proceeded ex parte against him.
7. The learned Tribunal based its conclusion on the spot panchanama.
The spot panchanama was exhibited before the learned Tribunal, as Exhibit 33.
A close reading of the same goes to show that,
the Car was severally damaged and the Truck was damaged on its driver side and gave dash to the Tree.
This gives rise to the only conclusion/inference that, the accident occurred due to fault of the Truck Driver.

The Exhibit 33 along with cross- examination of the Claimant no.2, leads to the only conclusion that, the accident was the result of rash and negligent driving of the Truck Driver and no other inference is possible.
The observations by the learned Tribunal in respect of the negligence 1 goes to show 6 FA97.2011.odt that, the evidence on record was not properly appreciated.
Hence, the following order:-
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed.
(ii) The findings of the learned Tribunal in respect of contributory negligence is quashed and set aside.
It is held that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Truck by its Driver.

(iii) The Respondent nos.4 and 5 shall jointly and severally pay the amount of Rs.62,500/- to the Claimants with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of Petition till its realisation with proportionate costs.
(iv) The amount deposited by the Appellant - Insurance Company under the impugned Judgment and Award in this Court shall be disbursed in favour of the Claimants along with interest accrued thereon.
